sections.h2: Which Union County offices deal with my tax bill?
sections.html:
Union County Tax Administration does, and its Revenue Division collects the bills. The Revenue Division is at 500 N. Main Street, Suite 119, Monroe, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 38, Monroe, NC 28111-0038 and a phone line at 704-283-3848.

Valuation questions and appeals go to the Tax Administrator's Office at 500 N. Main Street, Suite 236, or 704-283-3746. In person, the collector's counter in the Government Center takes payments weekdays from 8:00 in the morning to 5:00 in the evening.

The county also collects property tax bills for ten municipalities: Fairview, Hemby Bridge, Lake Park, Marshville, Marvin, Mineral Springs, Stallings, Waxhaw, Wesley Chapel and Wingate. A house inside one of those towns gets one combined collection through the county office. Ask the county which office bills a parcel inside a town not on that list.

sections.h2: How fast is Union County growing?
sections.html:
Growth stands out. QuickFacts estimates 267,674 residents in July 2025, 12.4% above the April 2020 base and the fastest pace of the four counties compared. The land area is 632.74 square miles, which gives 376.6 residents on each square mile.

The 2020-2024 median for owned homes is $417,300, and owners live in 81.6% of homes. Households earn a median $102,900. Census counts 95,683 housing units as of July 2025, with 2,707 permits issued for 2025, and rent in the middle is $1,496.

  • Persons per household: 2.95.
  • Degree holders: 40.5% hold a bachelor's or higher.
  • Foreign-born persons: 12.2%.
  • Average commute: 29.8 minutes each way.

Values in the county's last general reappraisal moved sharply, which is covered next.

sections.h2: How much did values move in the 2025 Union County revaluation?
sections.html:
It raised total taxable valuation from $32.38 billion in 2021 to $60.05 billion as of January 1, 2025, an increase of 60.05%. The county's results page lists residential up 63.45% and commercial and industrial up 45.59%.

Parcel counts grew from 104,057 in 2021 to 114,182 in 2025, per the county, while its median home value went from $293,377 to $403,000. The county's timeline runs as follows.

  • September 2024: community meetings on the reappraisal.
  • October 21, 2024: the schedule of values goes to the county commissioners.
  • November 4, 2024: public hearing, followed by adoption on November 18.
  • First week of March 2025: notices of new values.
  • April to July 2025: formal appeals heard, with a May 28 filing deadline.
  • June 2025: tax rate adopted with the budget.
  • August 2025: bills on the new values mailed.

For 2026, the county says it only sends a new notice when something changes on a property, such as new construction, an addition, demolition, a renovation, rezoning or an acreage change. For 2026, appeals opened January 1 and ended when that board adjourned on May 6, 2026. North Carolina requires counties to reappraise every eighth year, so ask the office about the next scheduled year.

sections.h2: What is the Union County billing and interest schedule?
sections.html:
Bills on real estate and personal property come due September 1, but no interest builds until after January 5. Mailed checks count if postmarked by that day, and a weekend January 5 pushes the cutoff to Monday.

Starting January 6, the county charges 2% through the end of the month, then three-fourths of 1% per month. Car and truck tax is collected when you register or renew a plate, so it stays off this bill.

Union County payment calendar, as the county prints it
DateWhat it means
September 1Bills fall due

January 6 to 312% interest
Each month afterAnother three-fourths of 1% monthly

Source: Union County Collection and Payment. Call the office for this year's rate and ask whether a prepayment discount applies.

sections.h2: What else does the Union County Revenue Division collect?
sections.html:
Property tax is only part of its workload. The county page lists the following among the charges handled by the division, and a closing agent may ask about any of them for the property you are selling.

  • Real estate and personal property tax bills.
  • Delinquent motor vehicle tax bills.
  • Gross receipts taxes.
  • Current and delinquent water and sewer bills.
  • Landfill fees and other utility payments.

The division also values every registered motor vehicle owned by a county resident. Call 704-283-3848 and ask whether any water, sewer or landfill balance sits on the account you are selling.

sections.h2: What payment options does Union County give?
sections.html:
The county page names five channels.

  • Mail: use the return envelope or write to P.O. Box 38, Monroe, NC 28111.
  • Drop box: on Stewart St. Extension, behind the Historic Post Office.
  • Phone: 1-855-497-0718.
  • Web: the county's pay online link.
  • Counter: the Government Center.

Sellers can route the current bill through the closing agent so the buyer gets a clean parcel. Ask the closer to request the payoff figure from the Revenue Division.

sections.h2: How does a Union County valuation appeal work?
sections.html:
An informal review with Tax Administration comes first, and a formal hearing before the county's equalization board follows if you still disagree. The county's appeal page says a staff appraiser reviews your evidence, mails a decision, and sends the case to the board if you return the form at the bottom of the decision letter.

The page describes the board as five citizens who hear your case and the staff's, and says it rules within 30 days. The board's letter explains how to continue to the statewide Property Tax Commission, and G.S. 105-290 sets 30 days from the mailing of the board's notice.

Useful evidence listed by the county includes appraisals as of the revaluation date, sales of similar properties, photos of unusual damage and letters about septic limits from Environmental Health or a licensed soil scientist. The percentage of change since a prior assessment cannot be considered. Both the informal review and the formal appeal are free, and a lawyer is not required.

sections.h2: Which relief programs can reduce a Union County bill?
sections.html:
State law offers three relief routes, and an owner may take only one. Each is requested from the county assessor on Form AV-9, and the form for 2026 prints the income limit at $38,800 and the upper circuit breaker band at $58,200.

  • An elderly or disabled exclusion under G.S. 105-277.1.
  • A disabled veteran exclusion under G.S. 105-277.1C, which NCDOR says has no age or income cap.
  • The circuit breaker under G.S. 105-277.1B, which limits tax to a share of income and defers the rest as a lien.

Ask Tax Administration which one fits and when to file. A sale ends eligibility for the circuit breaker, so deferred taxes become payable at closing.

sections.h2: What if a Union County house is sold with tax still due?
sections.html:
The debt travels with the land. G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien as of the listing date, with penalties, interest and costs, so buyers and lenders expect payoff at closing.

Continued nonpayment can lead to a foreclosure suit under G.S. 105-374, ending in a public auction at the courthouse door. Anyone redeeming before confirmation owes the taxes plus penalties, interest and costs.

In a quick sale, get the payoff from the Revenue Division, let the closer pay it out of the proceeds, and keep the receipt. The deed stamp tax is a separate charge to the seller, collected by the register of deeds before recording.

faqs.q: When does Union County need my tax payment?
faqs.a: September 1, with no interest until after January 5. Then 2% applies through January 31, followed by three-fourths of 1% monthly.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Union County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Go to the first-floor collector's counter at the Government Center on weekdays, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm. Letters go to the Monroe post office box.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 appeal window still open for Union County real estate?
faqs.a: No. The county says it closed with the board's May 6, 2026 adjournment. Ask Tax Administration about later years.

faqs.q: Does Union County have a veteran property tax exclusion?
faqs.a: Yes. State law shields the opening $45,000 of value for qualifying disabled veterans, filed with the county assessor.

faqs.q: Who owes deed stamp tax on a Union County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does, paying the register of deeds before recording. The amount appears on the settlement statement.
